_what: Which kept rows become journey steps (do-work/keep-steps.mjs). One mapping per kept table and step kind. where is the SQL that picks the rows, written over the table's own columns; each field is a SQL expression over the same row, named in fields: ref (the step's unique key, required), at (when the thing happened; rows are read from the newest kept step of this kind, comparing cutoff_column: the source row's own kept time, an insert time, against the newest journey step's insert time, so a row inserted late with an old event time is still kept), email (made into email_key in JavaScript and never kept raw), visitor (the journey visitor the row carries, when it does), offer_id, value_cents. source maps step source keys to fields. A payment_events row is scoped to the pursuit's own offers: a sale for an offer the pursuit does not sell keeps no step. A client with other table names gives its own mapping in the input, never a code branch.
_cutoff_overlap_minutes_what: A read starts this many minutes before the newest kept step's insert time, so a row whose transaction committed late (after a newer step was kept) is read again. Re-reading is harmless: a step with a ref already kept is left as it is.

mappings.where: event_kind = 'payment.confirmed' AND attributes->>'payment_status' = 'paid' AND attributes->>'offer_id' IN (SELECT id FROM offers)
